actioncam3000: At the depot, Gideon Actioncam had practised answering to his name. At R-F15, the first person to call it only wanted help with a crate.
The First Wave ribbon marked Gideon Actioncam as an early volunteer. At R-F15, a newcomer asked what those first days had been like.
A rat has started sitting on the ammunition box next to Gideon Actioncam's bunk. He has named it Bishop.
callmequeenorea_: Edmund Callmequeeno arrived at S-F16 with a carefully folded uniform. The first low beam corrected the cap; the first puddle corrected the rest.
Edmund Callmequeeno and Arno Olie sat through a quiet hour without finding anything to say. At relief, the next watch was told it had been a good hour.
csllgaks: On the way to S-F8, Dorian "Whistle" Csllgaks tried to memorise every turn. By the dugout door, he was simply glad someone else knew the way.
Stand-to at dawn. Dorian "Whistle" Csllgaks put a round across no man's land and the enemy line went quiet: Nils Wolfmananton, grazed.
A sneeze blew dust off the shelf above Dorian "Whistle" Csllgaks. This caused another sneeze and a discussion about moving the shelf.
julio.menezes921: Pavel Menezes introduced himself as a shepherd from Port Abel. The corporal repeated the name correctly. That helped more than the advice.
As one of the first hundred volunteers, Pavel Menezes received the First Wave ribbon. A neighbour lent the needle and supervised every stitch.
Pavel Menezes asked to leave the riflemans and serve as a signaller. The sergeant looked at him for a long time, then signed the paper without a word.
Pavel Menezes traded a book with the last pages torn out for two cigarettes and immediately regretted it.
Listening post, three in the morning. Pavel Menezes heard boots, then whispering, then nothing. Just a fox, the corporal said. He did not sleep afterwards.
